A Fleet Display That Cannot Lie — landed record

Closure synthesis for A Fleet Display That Cannot Lie: 356 committed run(s), 617 section-anchored comment(s), and 390 landed commit(s).

§1 — Why this is its own plan

doc-evidence · 2026-09-03T09:16:07.351Z

Cumulative evidence record created with an anchor per landed outcome, a dedicated anchor for each of the three corrections, and an outage-timeline figure; audit-doc clean

crew-token-quantities · 2026-09-08T06:06:24Z

Cumulative input and cumulative cached input are now separate named fields from the per-request peak, and neither dialect fills one from the other. The codex peak and input utilisation are the unmeasured marker rather than a sum, with the per-session rollout file named as the surface that does carry per-request figures. The multi-turn defect is closed in the same commit: usage accumulates over every measured completed turn instead of the last one winning, a usage-less terminal turn contributes nothing rather than letting a stale mapping stand, and budget input plus cached input now equals throughput cumulative input. Twenty importer and throughput-ledger files run one process per file on a debug partition: base 387 passed and 3 failed, head 394 passed and the same 3 failed, zero added.

crew-ledger-schema · 2026-09-08T06:11:19Z

Not a worker outcome, an infrastructure finding. The dispatch exposed that a roster member's declared harness never reaches backend selection, so a member registered for one lane silently ran on the default one. Stopped rather than allowed to consume the metered default lane. The node is redispatched to its intended lane through the per-dispatch flight override.

crew-ledger-schema · 2026-09-08T06:39:00Z

All fourteen previously undeclared keys are now in RECORD_FIELDS in the requested grouped order, and the static assertions naming each of them do run, so a future key cannot be added without the declaration failing. The drift-detection half does NOT run: the test finds no promoted rows in the worker environment and skips, which is what the brief told it to do and is a coordinator defect rather than a worker one. A test that skips where it executes provides no protection, which is the pattern this project already names for a disabled test. Repair queued: assert against the repository's own committed ledger, which is always present, rather than against globally mounted paths that a detached worktree cannot resolve. First spark row of the session: two commits, 21 minutes, the fully enumerated work delivered correctly and the brief followed literally including where it was wrong.

crew-routing-flag · 2026-09-08T06:49:34Z

A live dispatch can name its lane: --backend threads to the backend_override parameter that already existed, so the override inherits execution fit, sandbox reachability and write-path scope from the one path that performs them. A named-but-absent backend refuses instead of falling back to the default, and a member's declared harness now routes rather than being decorative. The run records the requested backend beside the resolved one, so a divergence is one grep instead of an accident. Importer census on a debug partition: base 27 failures, head the same 27, zero added. The worker notified the concurrent record-schema owner through the peer channel about its new record key rather than leaving it undeclared.

crew-lanes-view · 2026-09-08T07:25:19Z

The crew MCP tool has a lanes view reporting every configured endpoint's quota horizons, each carrying its own window length, remaining percentage, serving state and observation time, plus the effective context window and plan type. Horizons are keyed by window length rather than position, so a short-horizon figure cannot be published as a weekly one. Unreadable, unmetered and genuinely-zero are three distinguishable states. It reports availability and selects nothing, asserted by a test scanning the response for any field naming a chosen or preferred lane. Live route probe returned 10 of 10 configured backends. Focused gate 6 passed; importer delta on a debug partition across 33 files, 7 baseline failures and zero added.

crew-lane-disagreement · 2026-09-08T07:26:48Z

A flight override naming one lane against a member declaring another now refuses with both named, reported as the same error identity the named-backend disagreement already uses, so one situation has one behaviour regardless of which surface expressed the intent. The refusal populates no resolved agent block, which is the shape that let the silent override exist. Unchanged and pinned: an override against a member with no declared harness still routes, a member harness with no override still routes, and agreement still succeeds. Twelve routing-contract tests pass together with the predecessor's; importer census on a debug partition, base 27 identities and head the same 27, zero added; ruff 9 at base and 9 at head.

crew-serving-state · 2026-09-08T07:46:04Z

A lane near its ceiling and a lane whose reading is too old now report their own states instead of will-serve at every utilisation below the absolute ceiling. Both thresholds are declared with reasons rather than round numbers: at-risk at 94 percent because whole-percent quantisation leaves six distinguishable points before exhaustion, and stale after 47 minutes because that is under a sixth of the shortest reported 300-minute window. Staleness is evaluated before exhaustion, which is the correct order, since stale evidence cannot support a hold any more than it can support a clearance. Falsifiers include a full 0-to-100 utilisation sweep pinning the boundary, so the state ranges over the input domain rather than over the lanes that happen to exist, which is the failure mode that shipped a fail-open here earlier today. 13 tests pass and a bounded importer census reports 98.

crew-receipt-harvest · 2026-09-08T07:53:22Z

Promotion attaches the lane's quota reading, harvested by the harness from the client's own per-session receipt keyed by the recorded session id, to both the promotion result and the ledger row as a declared record field. The manifest is explicitly not a source, recorded as manifest_source_used false, which is the constraint that keeps the reading independent evidence of the run rather than the run's own claim about itself. Two independent horizons asserted, effective context window 121,600 on the fixture, a measured zero distinct from an unmetered lane, and a missing receipt non-fatal to promotion. Paired per-file set: base 61 passed and 9 failed, head 64 passed and 6 failed, zero added failure ids.

crew-state-typing · 2026-09-08T08:14:14Z

Worker states are typed by cause and each names its own recovery: a lane hold resumes, a failure redispatches, a needs-help is answered, a stall is investigated, a genuine block is decided, and an unwritten manifest resumes. Those first two were the costly pair, rendered identically before with opposite correct recoveries. A declared wait now outranks worker liveness, which closes the data-loss case: a parked run whose process had correctly exited was classified abandoned and fell out of the collection resume-ready walks, so nobody would have woken it. Both halves are pinned - the classification and the wait-set membership. An unsubstituted manifest template reads unwritten rather than terminal, so one early death stops holding a fence; in-progress is a declared non-terminal status so a mandated early write need not claim a terminal state; wait age is judged against the declared horizon; and a malformed wait is unreadable rather than abandoned. Base 7 failed and 270 passed, head the same 7 with 283 passed, identical ids and zero added.

crew-handoff-reading · 2026-09-08T08:16:02Z

A redispatched worker's prompt now states the inherited worktree as a reading taken at composition time - porcelain status, per-file summary, head commit and whether it differs from the recorded base - labelled with when it was taken and separated from the coordinator's advice, so a worker can tell a measurement from an instruction. Where the reading shows uncommitted changes the prompt carries the checkpoint instruction itself, which removes a class of coordinator error rather than one instance: the window between a coordinator's reading and the predecessor's stop cannot be closed by care, because the two cannot be simultaneous, and a handoff went stale inside it today on a single import line. A clean worktree is stated affirmatively rather than by omission, and an unreadable one is reported without refusing the handoff. Base 442 passed with 30 failed and 3 errors, head 448 passed with 24 failed and the same 3 errors, zero added ids.

crew-live-lanes · 2026-09-08T08:39:36Z

The lanes view probes for a live reading instead of reporting a stale one. The probe already existed and was never called: it runs the harness command's app-server transport and reads the account's rate limits, which runs no model and costs no quota. Every window the probe returns is now keyed by its own length rather than reduced to whichever is furthest through, and each row names whether a probe or that lane's own receipt described it, because the probe is keyed to the harness command and four lanes share one - which is why one lane was being reported with a sibling's utilisation. A probe that fails or times out degrades to the receipt path and says so. Nine tests, all probes stubbed; importer census base 98 passed and head 107 passed with zero failures either side.

crew-promotion-beat · 2026-09-08T08:28:57Z

The promotion result now carries a bounded fleet-state beat beside the quota reading: live runs, unreconciled runs, the actionable classifications present, occupied lanes, and its own observation time, derived from the existing live-pointer and drain reads rather than recomputed so the beat cannot drift from the views. Boundedness is asserted rather than intended - the same key set against a one-run fleet and a many-run fleet, with no list whose length varies. The ledger row is byte-identical with and without it, because a fleet snapshot does not describe the run the row records. Base 6 failures, head 6, zero added.

crew-mcp-reach · 2026-09-08T09:15:15Z

A dispatched codex worker CAN reach MCP servers from inside its own process: a luna worker called mcp__imas_dd__get_dd_versions with no approval required and quoted the tool's own response, giving a data-dictionary version range of 3.22.0 to 4.1.1 across 35 versions with 4.1.0 current. So briefs across this fleet can name authoritative lookups instead of asking a worker to infer facts. The unexpected result is what is absent: the worker saw 91 tools across three servers - imas_cx 37, codex_apps 36, imas_dd 18 - and ZERO reckon tools, although the host config declares a reckon server to that harness. The server starts standalone, the worker's stderr is empty and its stream carries no MCP error, so the cause is not established and must not be guessed; two of the reckon server's tools are configured to require an approval a non-interactive process cannot give, which is a candidate and not a finding. Consequence either way: a dispatched worker cannot read plans or crew state through MCP today.

crew-mcp-reach-terra · 2026-09-08T09:24:52Z

Tool reach confirmed on a second model of the family: the same data-dictionary tool, the same range 3.22.0 to 4.1.1 across 35 versions, 97 tools visible, no approval required. So reach is a harness property rather than a model one, which one lane's pass could not have established. The verbatim-spelling requirement paid for itself: three of the four declared servers expose their tools as mcp__server__tool and reckon alone exposes mcp__reckon_tool, because reckon's MCP tools are registered from module-private function names carrying a leading underscore that absorbs a separator. That irregularity is what defeated the coordinator's earlier pattern and made a present server read as absent, and the claude host spells the same tools differently again with three underscores.

crew-mcp-reach-sol · 2026-09-08T09:31:32Z

Third and final model of the metered family confirms tool reach: the same data-dictionary tool answered with the same range 3.22.0 to 4.1.1 across 35 versions, 97 tools visible, no approval required. All three models agree on the tool count exactly, which makes reach a harness property rather than a model one - the conclusion a single lane's pass could not have supported. All three also report reckon's five tools with a single separator against the double separator every other server uses, independently reproducing the irregularity that made a working server read as absent to a pattern match. The rename node was dispatched on that evidence.

crew-mcp-tool-names · 2026-09-08T09:54:55Z

All five reckon MCP tools publish regular wire names with no leading underscore, so each is addressed as mcp, server, double separator, tool exactly as the other three servers on this workstation are. The two host approval keys moved with them. The test walks the tool registry rather than naming five, so a sixth tool later is held to the same rule, and asserts the Python function names still carry their underscore, pinning that only the wire name moved. Five repaired importer files pass 93 tests; the full importer census reports 2 failures at base and the same 2 at head with zero added ids. The node blocked once on 26 added failures in seven test files the fence excluded, which was the coordinator's error for the second time today: a fence must include the tests that assert on the source it fences, or the census the node is required to produce is unproducible by construction.

crew-brief-points · 2026-09-08T10:04:38Z

A dispatch whose done-when reproduces a long contiguous span of its own plan section now quotes that span back to the coordinator on the dispatch result and records it on the run. The threshold is 23 words with the reason beside it - twenty-two words can still be one compact pointer naming a path, a symbol, a unit and a figure, and the twenty-third is where the text stops pointing and starts reproducing - swept across seven word counts from 20 to 26 so the boundary is pinned rather than asserted. It reports rather than refuses, because short shared facts are the pointing the rule wants and a blocking overlap check would invite being disabled. The legitimate-pointer falsifier carries a path, a symbol and a threshold together and must produce nothing. A reflowed paragraph is still caught, an unreadable section cannot break a dispatch, and a report changes no other field. This closes the enforcement gap on a rule written at sprint-orchestration.md line 449 that two coordinators broke seven times today.

crew-met-wait · 2026-09-08T10:26:29Z

A run whose declared wait has already reached a terminal state classifies as ready to resume and stays in the collection the resume sweep walks, instead of reading as a dead worker and leaving that collection. This was the data-loss case: a job that FINISHED left its run invisible to the sweep, so nobody would have woken it, and a peer recovered two by hand. The falsifier is a six-cell grid over liveness by condition state - alive and dead against pending, met and unknown - from one manifest fixture varying only those two inputs, because the previous falsifier varied liveness alone and every fixture it used had a pending condition, so the met case could not appear. A probe that errors, times out or returns something matching no terminal state is UNKNOWN and keeps the run waiting, never abandoned, since a probe failure says nothing about the worker; the classifier bounds the probe at one second so it stays a cheap read that cannot hang. Base 224 passed and 13 failed, head 236 passed and 1 failed, zero added ids.

crew-resume-baseline · 2026-09-08T14:26:52Z

Every attempt in a run's chain now shares the baseline recorded at that run's first dispatch, so an inherited manifest is read rather than discarded. This was the root cause under two symptoms already fixed today and unable to fire: a resumed run's baseline was captured from its predecessor attempt's manifest, so the inherited manifest's mtime equalled the baseline exactly, failed the newer-than test, and was treated as absent - measured at 1788874593998173197 on both sides of one run at attempt six whose file read status waiting with five well-formed wait fields. Four of five live runs in a peer fleet were affected, not one: the parked case classified abandoned and left the resume sweep, while three with terminal statuses classified running, which is the same discard with a harmless-looking outcome. The gate keeps its real job, asserted separately: a manifest predating the run entirely is still not credited as this attempt's outcome. Eight-cell grid over attempt number by manifest status. Base 123 passed and 10 failed, head 132 passed and 1 failed, zero added ids.

The remainder is a routing judgement with its figures, not an omission. Five landed nodes are verified by this coordinator, merged, and pushed; what they lack is the independent review that gates their ledger record, not their correctness. Dispatching five more reviews was declined on measurement: the locally served lane carries 17 live workers host-wide, and the metered lane reads 26% of its weekly window used at burn 1.65× with projected exhaustion 2026-09-18T22:10 against a reset of 2026-09-21T05:57 — so at today's rate it runs out two and a half days before the window turns over. Neither lane should absorb five more nodes for bookkeeping, and the burn figure moved from 1.44× to 1.65× over this session's own codex routing, which is the cost being reported rather than hidden.

The review gate earned its place and that is the session's main result. Three reviews ran; all three found a real defect in work this coordinator had personally verified and merged — an unauthorised silence checked off against the wrong clause, a regex never probed against prose, a naming rule not applied to a subject line. Two produced repairs that landed the same session. None was a worker being careless; all three were a careful reader's blind spots, which is the case the saturated worker-authored gate could never make.

The recurring defect has one shape and now has seven instances. A change correct in its own surface meets a second surface written under the older assumption, and the contradiction is visible only at the seam — where every test written for the first surface still passes. The landing grant against the read-only tier, the test role's repository paths, the documentation tier, the peer-scope disclosure, promotion serialising behind a plan's slowest worker, the scoring lifecycle unable to close itself, and a resume relaunching on a lane its own record does not name. Worth stating as one class because the fix for each was cheap and the finding for each cost a session.

# crew-observability-truth — currency report at main revision 1c20ca680a2b35119f6256431c5c62ef53b7bc34

Scope: the seven `data-status="open"` followups in the plan and the nine sections its
`plan-section-declarations` meta declares `implementable` (s1, s12, s14, s15, s17,
s18, s19, s21, s22; the roadmap's implementable set is exactly that filter,
`reckon/roadmap.py:100-108`). All file:line citations are from the committed blob at
the revision above (tree clean; `git rev-parse HEAD` == `git rev-parse origin/main`).
Measure at main: cohort of seven plan-surface test files — 207 passed, exit 0
(`logs/cohort.log`); no repository file was changed, so base and head are identical.

## Verdicts

### Open followups

**1. f-cot-a-pointer-field-lags-the-authority-it-mirrors — PARTLY MET.**
- Met half (resumability readers): the resolver exists and composes three sources in
  order — `reckon/crew/resumption.py:398-404` (`SESSION_SOURCES = ("pointer",
  "stream", "ledger")`), `_pointer_session` :403, `_stream_session` :406 with the
  incident written into its docstring, `resolve_session` :462. Recovery classification
  consumes `session_resolution`, not the raw field: `reckon/crew/recovery.py:5667-5707`;
  the pointer carries it from dispatch: `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7553`.
- Unmet half (retry fence): `failure_attribution` is referenced nowhere in
  `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, `recovery.py` or `observe.py` (grep returns nothing at
  main), so the fence cannot read it. The fence itself is
  `needs_help_after_failures` at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4963`, counting failures
  without the scaffolding/substance distinction the followup asks for.
- Reproduction a repair starts from: `grep -rn failure_attribution reckon/crew/` (empty),
  then assert the composed prompt/fence consults the manifest's `failure_attribution`
  key; write paths: `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, `reckon/crew/prompts/` (prompt source),
  `tests/test_crew_prompts.py`.

**2. f-cot-the-review-record-outlives-only-half-of-what-it-claims — UNMET.**
The verbatim text still does not reach the ledger row, and no code path drops the
claim. Executed check (run at main, `logs/ledger_review.log`):
`docs/state/reckon/crew.json` holds 2,042 runs, 431 with a non-null `review`; every
such row's review object has keys `{absent, scores, status, total}` and no `raw_text`.
`raw_text` is written only by the review store: `reckon/crew/review.py:418`. So the
row survives config loss with the scores and not the evidence, exactly the measured
state the followup describes. Write paths a repair needs: `reckon/ledger.py` and the
row-composition in `reckon/crew/promotion.py` (or the plan text that makes the claim),
plus a test. The followup prefers dropping the claim if carrying the text is
expensive; that is a lead/design choice, not a repair.

**3. f-cot-the-wait-predicate-settled-by-three-corrections — MET.**
Both repair halves landed and one executed check covers them.
- Half one: `reckon/crew/recovery.py:4204 _declared_wait_age_seconds` — ages a
  declared wait from the later of its declaration and the run's last stream write,
  with the 1804 s incident in its docstring.
- Half two: `reckon/crew/recovery.py:3500 _wait_probe_is_a_no_op` — refuses a probe
  that "can report nothing but success", landed in commit `de8b5e8dc` (2026-09-18,
  ancestor of main), extended by `a466546bc`.
- Executed check: `tests/test_wait_marker_is_not_a_stub.py` 37 cases green in the
  cohort run (`logs/cohort.log`, 207 passed).
- The remaining item — whether a stale wait should expire rather than age — is stated
  in the followup as a design question for the lead, not a repair; it is the only
  part still open.

**4. f-cot-arrival-resume — MET.**
The gate case now passes: `tests/test_transition_extraction.py:348
test_a_rendered_row_without_a_source_state_is_still_an_arrival` (and :323
`test_a_rendered_transition_row_is_read_not_guessed`) green, 9 passed exit 0
(`logs/arrivals.log`). The fix commit `f17ab71c` ("read an arrival rendered with no
source state") is an ancestor of main; the extraction entry point is
`reckon/crew/query.py:808 extract_watch_arrivals`.

**5. f-cot-worker-scratch-dirties-every-worktree — UNMET.**
gc still sees harness scratch as dirt. `reckon/crew/routing.py:530` runs
`git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` in `_tree_state` (:510) and
records every entry (`status_entries`, :559-568); no code excludes `codex-home/` or
`harness/` — the only occurrence of `codex-home` in `reckon/` is the backend's
`CODEX_HOME` name at `reckon/_backends.py:1916`. `garbage_collect`
(`reckon/crew/routing.py:818`) feeds that state into `_inspect_workspace` (:594).
- Smallest reproduction a repair starts from: create a temp repo with one merged
  branch, add a worktree, plant `codex-home/` and `harness/` untracked, call
  `reckon.crew.routing.garbage_collect(repo=<tmp>, apply=False)` and assert
  `classification == "integrated"` (it will read otherwise at main).
- Write paths: `reckon/crew/routing.py`, `tests/test_crew_gc.py`.

**6. f-cot-s21-decomposed-into-five-nodes — PARTLY MET.**
- N2 (sub-floor disposition has a command) landed after the followup was written:
  `record_dimension_disposition` (`reckon/crew/review.py:1554`) now has a production
  caller at `reckon/cli.py:4222`; merge `5c91163b` is an ancestor of main.
- M6 (dimensions on the committed row) landed: 431 of 2,042 ledger rows carry
  `review.scores` (executed check above).
- M1/M7 (a reader; score queryable from committed state) exist as the crew MCP
  `view="scores"` surface reading rows by plan/node/run_id.
- M4 (per-role rubric for worker reviews) and M5 (owning actor per dimension) are not
  landed: `grep owning_actor|per_role` finds nothing in `reckon/crew/review.py`; the
  rubric machinery there (:101-153) is the plan-review rubric, not a worker rubric
  keyed by role.
- N3/N4/N5 and the floor values wait on lead decisions, as the followup states.

**7. f-cot-lane-counts-parity-and-remaining-names — PARTLY MET.**
- Unmet half: the parity case still resolves both sides through one reader —
  `tests/test_lane_reading_carries_counts.py:263-269`
  (`read_lane_counts(written) == {"generating": reading["generating"], "waiting":
  reading["waiting"]}`, test `test_the_document_reader_returns_the_counts_the_payload_carries`,
  :236). A regression inside `read_lane_counts` moves both sides; the case cannot fail.
  Smallest reproduction: mutate `reckon/crew/lane_document.py:399 read_lane_counts` to
  return e.g. `generating: -1` and run that single case — it stays green at main.
- Second half appears already satisfied and the cited lines are stale: at main
  `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3028` is the only document read and it goes through
  `_lane_document.read_lane_counts`; the literals at :2912-2913 are payload defaults
  for an unmeasured lane, not document reads. (Inspected, not proved by mutation.)
- Write paths: `tests/test_lane_reading_carries_counts.py` (assert against literal
  fixture counts); `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` only if a document read is still found.

### Implementable sections

**§1 — no unmet work of its own; it is F1's landing home.** The body is the plan's
rationale (docs/plans/crew-observability-truth.html §1) and carries no measure; its
only actionable content is F1's two halves, whose verdicts are above.

**§12 — PARTLY MET.** Most measures landed (`9a2f95e`, `8417c0f`, `9c51724b`,
`d0956c85`, `9bb8b7c7`, `0d3c6cf5`, `ca539bcc`, `dc60bae3`, `dbd96dbd`, `92be14fd`,
`1f519333`, `eb74752d`, `2a94b12c`, `52c04865`, all ancestors), and its followup
F4 is now met. The outstanding half is the one its own landed summary names: the
promotion guard still swallows a parse refusal —
`reckon/crew/promotion.py:278-283` (`parse_manifest(...)` inside

§4 — What a person should be able to read off the pane

impl-fit · 2026-09-03T08:08:56.320Z

Killed by the claude account's individual spend limit, reset 12pm Europe/Paris; the stream's terminal event was type result subtype success carrying the refusal text, so nothing classified it as a failure

reckon-ship · 2026-09-03T08:17:00+00:00

The canonical instance of this section's obligation, produced by this plan's own execution and caught by the lead rather than by the tooling — which is the fourth time that sentence has been true in this fleet's history. At 10:07 the claude account reached an individual spend limit resetting 12pm Europe/Paris. Five workers on that lane died within seconds of each other. Ten minutes later the pane read 6 working, and the coordinator had just written to the lead that it was waiting on five workers that were already dead. Four independent detectors each failed for a different reason, and every one is already named somewhere in this sprint. First, the stream's terminal event was type result with subtype success, the refusal text sitting in the result field — a provider refusal recorded as a completion, so nothing downstream had a failure to classify. Second, all five died at phase starting and never advanced to working, and the stall and terminal-manifest checks evaluate over the literal working phase, so the runs were permanently ineligible for the check that would have caught them; that is clive-local-workers §7's finding verbatim, reported there by another session and reproduced here. Third, log_age_seconds read 383 with log_fresh true, because freshness is file mtime and the file had been touched by system records after the last generation event — this section's activity-is-generation rule, failing in the direction it predicts. Fourth, the classification was derivable the whole time: crew observe produced dispatched to abandoned for all five the moment it was asked, so the follower had nothing wrong with it and nothing asked. The measurement that separated live from dead took one read of each stream: the surviving run had its last assistant turn at record 333 of 334, the dead ones had a rate_limit_event followed by the refusal. That is the check the display should be making.

reckon-ship · 2026-09-03T08:22:00+00:00

A second finding from the same check, in another direction, and it is not this project's to fix. CORRECTING MY OWN CORRECTION, which had the right verdict and the wrong mechanism, and the wrong mechanism prescribed a remedy that would have prevented nothing. I attributed the false reachability finding above to a stale remote-tracking ref and prescribed fetching before judging. Verified independently at the peer's prompting and the peer is right: every entry in git reflog show refs/remotes/origin/main reads update by push, with no fetch entry anywhere, because this checkout carries 20 worktrees over one common ref store at Code/reckon/.git — so a push moves the remote-tracking ref directly and there is nothing to fetch. Fetch-before-judging is hygiene for a separate clone or CI where the ref genuinely lags; here it would have changed the answer by nothing. The actual mechanism is shelf life. The merge commit was created 10:46:24, the ref moved to it at 10:49:05, and the finding was authored 10:50:27 — so the check ran before 10:49:05, when not-reachable was the CORRECT answer, and was published at least 82 seconds after it stopped being true, into a wave putting four pushes on this branch in 21 minutes. The measurement was right and the prose outlived it. So the measure changes shape rather than gaining a fetch: reachability is a reading with a shelf life, not a fact, and promotion must re-derive it in the same beat as it records the verdict and stamp it with that instant, because an unstamped reachability claim gives a reader no way to tell whether it has expired. ONE REFINEMENT THE EXCHANGE EXPOSED AND NEITHER OF US NAMED: reachable is ambiguous between merged-locally and pushed, and the two answers differed by three minutes here. The peer judged against origin/main, which answers is it pushed; my promotion claimed merged, which was true of local main from 10:46:24. Both readings were correct about different questions. So the recorded verdict must name the ref it was taken against, or it is untestable by the next reader even when stamped.

A STORED CLASSIFICATION CARRIES NO OBSERVATION TIME, so a stale verdict and a current one are indistinguishable — contributed by session imas-codex-75, verified here rather than accepted, and it is the fourth direction the same defect has appeared from today. Their measured cost: a bug that had already been fixed read as live for thirteen minutes and produced a confident wrong diagnosis from them. Verified independently: classify_pointer returns terminal_at, terminal_age_seconds and log_age_seconds, so its INPUTS carry ages, and the verdict it returns carries no stamp of its own. The pointer's stored phase likewise carries none, which is why this surface's own guidance already warns that phase lags the stored record and tells readers to prefer the computed classification — advice that exists precisely because the stored one cannot be dated and therefore cannot be trusted. This is distinct from §7, which requires an age on every BUDGET reading; the same property is missing on the classification store, and a reader has no way to notice. Two remedies, and the first is cheaper than it looks: stamp the classification when it is stored so a reader can compare it against now, or drop the stored verdict entirely and make every reader recompute, which is what the guidance already recommends informally. Recording the pattern across the day, because four instances in one session is a shape rather than a coincidence: a reachability check compared a commit against a remote ref whose age nobody could see; a budget hold blocked seventeen dispatches on evidence three hours nineteen minutes old; an availability record read clear on evidence seven hours old and was right by luck; and now a classification verdict cannot be dated at all. Every one is a reading that was correct when taken and false when used. The generalisation this plan should carry is that a stored judgement without a timestamp is not a judgement, it is a rumour — and that applies to every store in this surface, not to the four that happened to be caught.

New measure added to this section from a defect measured live in this session: a durable manifest is not a terminal one. The manifest-before-the-wait discipline exists because a print-mode worker gets no turn after its last one, so a worker must write its manifest before starting a long wait - but the only non-terminal status word available is blocked. Four of this session's twelve runs wrote status blocked with blockers naming their own pending implementation, were classified blocked, emitted that reason to every follower, and were working normally with logs seconds old; two later transitioned blocked to working unprompted and one blocked to promoted. So the display cannot distinguish a placeholder from a worker that has genuinely stopped and needs answering, which is the one distinction the blocked bucket exists to make. Recorded as a measure rather than a comment so roadmap gates on it, per the rule that same-plan discovered work becomes a section on a live plan rather than a followup.

FINDING CONTRIBUTED BY THE IMAS-AMBIX SESSION, written as content and deliberately not filed into this tree because it had caused a collision here earlier the same day. A WRITE FENCE COVERS THE MECHANISM IT WAS DESIGNED FOR, NOT THE ACTOR STANDING OUTSIDE IT. Three instances on 2026-09-05, all surfacing as a REFUSED MERGE rather than as any alert, and in each the protection was real, correctly implemented, and enumerating the wrong population. Instances 1 and 2, a tool inside a worktree resolving a path into the shared checkout: run r-20260905T141745440369-dsv4-endpoint-publish touched imas_ambix/agent/cli.py and tests/test_agent_endpoint_discovery.py outside its fence, and r-20260905T160558234233-dsv4-dryrun-port-order touched imas_ambix/agent/cli.py and tests/test_agent.py, both leaving edits in the main checkout rather than their own detached worktrees, both merges refused with please commit your changes or stash them before you merge. Two unrelated nodes, two different declared scopes, neither naming the main checkout; both had run a formatter; diffs of 51 and 106 lines, both AST-identical to HEAD, captured outside the repository before being discarded. Instance 3 is the one that hit this repository: a coordinator hand-editing skills/reckon-ship/SKILL.md while a crew run held that exact path as its exclusive write scope. THESE GENERALISE PAST THIS SECTION'S EXISTING MEASURE. Write exclusivity is per repository, not per project assumes the writers are RUNS. These three say the writer set is larger than the run set in two independent directions: downward into the tools a run invokes, and sideways to sessions that never dispatched at all. Instances 1 and 2 are the stronger pair precisely because nothing in the dispatch contract could prevent them - a worktree is a directory, not a jail, and a path resolving out of it is ordinary filesystem behaviour. THE HAZARD IS NOT THE FORMATTING. Formatting announces itself; a semantic edit by the same route would not, and a coordinator would then integrate one state while the shared tree quietly held another. MEASURES, and the second is the subtle one: git -C status --porcelain is empty at the moment a coordinator merges a worker commit, which both formatter instances would have failed; a stray path is classified by AST identity against HEAD rather than by diff size or by looking like formatting, because cmp and wc -l answer the wrong question and a semantic edit can be two lines; and the scope validator states its own population in its output, so a reader sees that it covers runs and not hand edits rather than inferring a guarantee it does not make. THEIR CAVEAT, KEPT DELIBERATELY: two instances of the tool escape and one hand edit, from a single day and one project. The mechanism is general; the RATE is not established, and no frequency claim belongs in this plan. Tested the first measure here while two workers were live: reckon's checkout carried one dirty plan file from a promotion comment, and both workers' output was correctly confined to their own worktrees. So the assertion is cheap, it fires, and it fired on a benign case - which is the right behaviour for a check whose value is that it also catches the malign one.

FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE FENCE-NAMES-ITS-POPULATION MEASURE, on reckon's own shadow surface, contributed by the imas-ambix session and verified here structurally. A SHADOW WORKER CAN READ THE ANSWER IT IS BEING MEASURED ON. crew shadow re-runs a committed node at its original base as never-merged evidence, but a worktree shares the object store with its parent checkout, so a base ref predating the landed commit does not hide that commit: git log on main, then git show the sha, and the answer is in hand. Verified here rather than reasoned - from a worktree created at an older base, git cat-file -t on the current HEAD sha returns commit and git log renders its subject. MEASURED, NOT THEORISED, by a peer running a repeat measurement across two deployments from a base deliberately chosen to predate the landing. The worker found the landed commit through the shared repository, reproduced it byte-identically in both files, and said so in its manifest; its gate passed 12 of 12. First edit came at turn 60 after 463 seconds against turn 6 at 17 seconds for the original run, because the interval had been spent reading rather than solving - so the time-to-first-edit comparison was void and the output tokens measured transcription. Promoted with the contamination stated and not merged, which is the right disposal. WHY IT IS THIS MEASURE AND NOT A METHODOLOGY NOTE: the fence is --base, and what it fences is the WORKTREE'S CHECKOUT STATE, not the WORKER'S REACHABLE KNOWLEDGE. It names one population, the files at that revision, and the worker reads from a larger one. HOW IT DIFFERS FROM THE FORMATTER PAIR, and the distinction is theirs: there the escape is an unconstrained filesystem and nothing in the dispatch contract could prevent it, while here the escape is git's own design, so a fix is at least conceivable - the object store is shared deliberately and for good reasons, and it is the REACHABILITY of a later ref rather than the sharing that leaks. CANDIDATE ASSERTION, offered tentatively by its author and recorded as tentative: a shadow's evidence is clean only if the answer is unreachable from its worktree, so the check is whether the node's own landed commit is an ancestor of anything reachable there rather than whether HEAD sits at the recorded base. crew shadow records nothing of the kind today. Recording it beside the result may be sufficient rather than enforcing it, since a reader who knows the answer was reachable can discount the row without the system preventing the run - and prevention may not be achievable while the object store is shared.

THE REFUSAL-VISIBILITY GAP IS WIDER THAN THIS PLAN RECORDED: IT COVERS PROMOTION, NOT ONLY DISPATCH. Routed by another project's coordinator, who measured it promoting a single node through four attempts, each refused for a different and entirely legitimate reason — a gate lacking the check that produced it, a manifest missing its commits field, uncommitted changes at a declared path in the main checkout, and a changed path outside the declared write scope. None of the four produced a follower event. The run sat at unpromoted throughout and the pane's only line for the whole promotion was the final unpromoted → promoted. A reader of that stream sees a clean two-step and no evidence that promotion was ever contested.

Every refusal was correct behaviour — reckon declining to record evidence it could not verify. The finding is not that they happened; it is that the pane cannot show that they happened.

The asymmetry has a structural cause, and it is why no amount of care fixes it. A success is self-announcing: the work exists and the next read finds it. A refusal creates nothing, so there is no run to hang a transition on, so the stream is structurally silent — the coordinator's return value is the only witness, and only if it is read. That is tolerable one call at a time and degrades with batch width, which is the direction this fleet has been pushed. The original narrower instance: a dispatch refused for per-member serialisation inside a wave of six, where the pane showed five arrivals and was silent about the sixth request. Had the pane been trusted, 42 plans of an exhaustive triage would have been left silently uncovered.

Deliberately recorded without a proposed mechanism, on the reporter's reasoning, which is sound: a stream carrying non-events is a different kind of unreliable. A refusal counter a coordinator can compare against what it intended to send, or simply documenting that the stream cannot carry refusals so the return value must be read, are both plausible — as is judging the exposure acceptable. What would not work is a coordinator-side convention, because that is the compensation this project keeps finding does not survive a context boundary.

One correction the reporter volunteered against their own account, worth keeping because it protects the monitor from a false charge: the follower did fire correctly, 90 seconds after the run went terminal. The 36-minute delay that followed was the coordinator seeing the event, saying it would gate the run, and answering something else first. The instrument worked; the reader did not.

A QUERY AGAINST A FIELD THAT DOES NOT EXIST RETURNS EXACTLY WHAT A REAL ABSENCE RETURNS, AND NOTHING IN THE RESULT DISTINGUISHES THEM. This section already records that absence of evidence has been mistaken for evidence three times in this fleet's history. Three more happened today, between two coordinators, in one session-day — so the count is not the point and the shape is. All three share one structure: a payload nobody had looked at, a uniform empty result, and a confident reading of it.

ReadingActual causeWhat it nearly cost
every live pointer walked for a top-level write_paths key; uniform emptythe key does not exist at that levelreported every path free, including two a peer was actively holding
the ledger queried for a records key; zero rowsthe key is runsabout to report that a promotion had not recorded
manifest_error: None beside a precise parser refusalthe view carries no manifest detail at all — all 13 rows, every manifest field absenta fabricated finding, asserted twice and passed to a peer as corroboration

The first row is the one that shows the stakes. A scope reading that reports free paths which are in fact held does not produce a wrong document — it produces two workers writing one file. The other two cost a retraction; that one would have cost work.

The detector is one command and it is the only reliable one: does ANY row carry this field. A positive control distinguishes the two cases and nothing else does — not the shape of the result, not its plausibility, not the code that should have written it. That last point is the sharp one, contributed by the peer who made two of the three: checking the capture code is a check on the writer when the doubt belongs on the reader. In the third instance here the capture was verified correct, and the reading was still wrong, because the question was never whether the value was written but whether the view returns it.

Why it survives being known. All three readers knew the rule; one of them had recorded it in this plan the same morning. It defeats knowing it because the empty result confirms the expectation that prompted the query — you go looking for a silence and you find one — and at that moment the expectation and the evidence are the same object. The control is cheap precisely because it does not test the hypothesis: it tests the instrument, which is the thing under suspicion and the thing never suspected.

THE UNREADABLE CLASSIFICATION FIRES ON THE NORMAL MANIFEST AUTHORING SEQUENCE, AND THIS COORDINATOR WATCHED IT HAPPEN THIS MORNING WITHOUT RECORDING IT AS A DEFECT. Measured by a peer:

10:10:25Z   manifest written (orientation block)
10:10:28Z   follower: unreadable — "repair: the manifest at ..."
10:13:00Z   manifest parses: status 'waiting', cleanly

Three seconds. The worker writes the orientation block first and the status line after — exactly as the contract instructs, manifest before any long wait — and the classifier sampled the gap between two writes. Nothing was wrong at any point.

This session saw the identical thing at 05:10 and read it as benign without recording it. The landing-grant run reported cannot read manifest: the body reads as manifest fields (node, orientation_base_sha, orientation_worktree, orientation_write_paths) but carries no status key, and it was noted in passing as the orientation block the worker writes first; it will resolve when it writes a status. That diagnosis was correct and the conclusion drawn from it was wrong: knowing why a display is lying is not the same as the display not lying, and a coordinator who did not happen to know the authoring order would have opened a worktree.

Two populations, one state, and no reader repair reaches the second. A manifest unreadable because a worker decorated its status word is the six-form defect repaired this session. A manifest unreadable because it is three seconds old is not a spelling at all. They produce the same row and the same instruction.

The general shape, and it is the third instance today. A run finished, merged and pushed displayed as stalled. A three-second-old manifest displayed as unreadable with a repair prompt. A starved worker indistinguishable from a hung one, which had three coordinators opening raw streams by hand. Different causes, one shape: a state derived from a single sample of something that changes, announced as though it were settled. Every one of the three told a reader to act where acting was wasted, and in two of them the reader was about to destroy working work.

The discriminator needs no new state. Requiring a condition to survive one observation interval before it becomes actionable drops the transient population entirely while leaving a genuinely undecodable manifest exactly as loud — the file's own age against the run's would do as well. That is a property of the classifier rather than the reader, so it is not covered by the six-form repair and not covered by the classifier node now in flight, whose measures are about a dead process against a terminal manifest. It is a third sibling.

unknown · undated

A positive control for the honest-unknown form, found by nearly filing a defect against it. Ahead of an authorised serve restart that would kill every in-flight local worker, recovery depended on each run's session_id. Read straight off the live pointer files, 20 of 28 are null — which reads as a fleet that is 71% unrecoverable. I reported that to two peer sessions; one relayed it onward, where it rescued a run a third session had already written off as needing redispatch.

The rescue was right and the framing was wrong. crew list does not show what the pointer files show: its session_resolution block consults pointer → stream → ledger and resolves 24 of 25. The one it cannot resolve it reports exactly as this plan argues a surface should — resolved: false, source: None, and the detail "all three were consulted, so this is an absence rather than a reading nobody has taken yet." A genuine absence, distinguished in words from a reading not yet taken.

So the charge that a surface was stating a falsehood does not land, and a proposed repair was withdrawn before anyone acted on it. reckon/crew/AGENTS.md already records the underlying hazard and what it cost twice in one day; what is new is that the fix for it is in place and works.

The hazard has therefore moved, and this is the part worth carrying: it is no longer a display that misleads, it is a coordinator reading around the display to the raw store underneath. Both peers and I independently ran the same shortcut. A surface cannot defend against being bypassed — so wherever a raw record is load-bearing and its resolved form lives elsewhere, the raw field is the thing that needs to stop being readable as an answer, not the surface that needs fixing.

THE UNIT. _ClaudeDialect._budget in reckon/_backends.py reads info.get('utilization') and assigns float(utilisation) straight into utilisation_pct. That field is a FRACTION: an overage record reads 1.21 meaning 121 percent, and a five-hour window reads 0.61 meaning 61 percent. A five-hour window at 99 percent would read 0.99 percent. The fence cannot fire on this lane at any utilisation. THE FIELD. The gating quantity is unifiedWindows..utilization against that window's own resetsAt, not the top-level account figure, whose resetsAt of 2026-10-01 is a calendar-month boundary. unifiedWindows appears seven times in this repository and every one is inside tests/fixtures/backends/claude-worked-turn.jsonl, carrying five_hour utilization 0.61 - the correct field is sitting in our own fixture, unread by the parser that fixture feeds. The usedPercent path in the same module is the codex account surface, a genuine percent, handled correctly, which is why codex reads a sane 46 percent while claude reads 1.21. THE ACCOUNT. claude and claude-opus keep separate budget records for one account - 47 and 16 records here, both landing on 1.21 overage nine minutes apart - so an observation on one preset teaches the other nothing. WHY THIS OUTRANKS THE OTHER FLIGHT-LAYER ITEMS, and the relaying session's argument is right: the failure is asymmetric in the dangerous direction. A stale hold is self-announcing, because the fleet stops and someone investigates within minutes. A stale clearance is silent - the wave opens, every turn refuses, and the runs read as worker failures rather than as a fence that never fired. That is the silent-success shape this repository keeps paying for.

A WORKING ESCAPE FROM A SELF-SUSTAINING STALE HOLD, measured by the imas-ambix session and worth more than the diagnosis, which was already documented. The hazard is recorded in this workstation's guidance: only a served run writes a budget record, and a hold blocks every run, so once recorded nothing clears it. What was not recorded anywhere is how to get out. Two things that did NOT work, both tried: closing the hold record, because preflight re-derives from ledger evidence rather than reading a hold flag; and setting budget_check false, which stops the check without refreshing the evidence the check reads. WHAT WORKED: --set budget.resume_reserve_pct=0 for a single dispatch, which let one run be served, and that run wrote fresh evidence. 95 percent stale became 35 percent real. The mechanism is exactly right - the reserve exists so a spent quota keeps enough headroom to answer a stuck worker, and zeroing it for one deliberate dispatch spends that reserve to buy a fresh observation, which is the only thing that can break the loop. Their suggestion stands and I would put it beside the record-format-version finding above rather than as a separate item: an operator-facing way to mark evidence superseded. Both are the same defect - a budget observation carries no provenance and no way to be retired, so it can be wrong indefinitely and can be self-sustaining while wrong. The reserve-zeroing escape is a workaround for the second half; the parser-version stamp would fix the first.

CORRECTION TO THE ENTRY ABOVE, from its author, and it matters because I recorded a remedy without the precondition that makes it work. --set budget.resume_reserve_pct=0 IS NOT A GENERAL ESCAPE from a stale hold. It worked in that instance because the recorded utilisation was EXACTLY 95.0 against an effective ceiling of 95 - the ceiling being 100 less the 5 percent resume reserve - so dropping the reserve moved the ceiling to 100 and 95.0 cleared it. On a lane recording 99 percent, or recording a real 95 rather than a stale one, it does nothing, and it SHOULD do nothing: the reserve exists so a spent quota keeps enough headroom to answer a stuck worker, and a flag that spent it on a genuinely exhausted lane would be a way to lose the last of a quota rather than a way to recover an instrument. So the arithmetic was a coincidence of that reading, not a mechanism. WHAT TRANSFERS is the diagnosis plus one sentence: get a single turn served on the lane by any legitimate means, because only a served run writes fresh evidence and that is the sole thing that breaks the loop. Two things that do NOT work, both tried and both worth knowing because they are what a reader reaches for first: closing the hold record, since preflight re-derives from ledger evidence rather than reading a hold flag; and setting budget_check false, which stops the check without refreshing the evidence the check reads. The general fix remains the one recorded above - an operator-facing way to mark evidence superseded, beside the record-format version - and this correction strengthens the case for it, because the only current escape is a coincidence of arithmetic that a reader could easily generalise into losing a reserve they needed.

Its resume-1.jsonl opens with this session was recorded with model gpt-5.6-luna but is resuming with gpt-5.6-sol, the provider then refused the turn, and the run returned to a dead process with its manifest unchanged.

Root cause, read in source. resume_plan takes its backend from _backend_settings (dispatch.py:3840), which returns only argv[0] — the bare command — and says why in its own docstring: only the command matters for reading. That is true for reading a stream and false for relaunching one, and resume_plan reuses it to relaunch. So the command survives and the model is re-resolved from config, which on this workstation means the project default.

The remedy is already in the record it is reading. A live pointer's argv, measured here:

["codex","exec","--json","-C",…,"-m","gpt-5.6-sol","-c","model_reasoning_effort=high",…]

The -m flag is present in the same argv the resume already parses for argv[0]. Reusing the recorded model rather than re-resolving it keeps a resumed session on its own lane with no flag from the caller.

The confirmation that makes this more than a mismatch: there is no workaround. The reporter re-issued with --backend codex-luna and it was refused as already uses backend codex-luna — while that same relaunch ran gpt-5.6-sol. The refusal proves the run record holds the right lane; the relaunch proves the launch path ignores it. The two halves disagree at exactly the seam, and because the override is rejected as a no-op a caller cannot force the correct model by any means. A resume of a non-default-lane run is therefore not merely mis-routed, it is unrepairable from outside.

A second half of the report is recorded as reported-not-reproduced: that a resumed turn refused at the provider before any tool call leaves the run classified running-then-dead with no follower line naming the refusal, findable only by reading resume-N.jsonl. THE SECTION'S SECOND MEASURE DEMONSTRATED ITSELF WITHIN MINUTES OF BEING WRITTEN, AND THE HOLD TURNS OUT TO BE SELF-SUSTAINING. Measured 2026-09-03 at 10:15:58Z. A dispatch to the claude lane was refused budget-hold at utilisation 100.0 percent, type spend-limit, threshold exhausted, source live-run. Three readings from the same payload settle it. The evidence is stamped observed_at 10:02:01Z while the pre-flight ran at 10:15:58Z, so the refusal rests on a reading fourteen minutes old. resets_at is None, so §6's unparsed-reset gap means the fence cannot even compute whether the stated reset has passed. And a live one-token probe at the same moment returned is_error false with a served answer. The record said exhausted, the endpoint said yes, and the record won — which is the measure a-stale-hold-is-re-derived-not-obeyed, failing in exactly the shape it was written to forbid. THE DEADLOCK IS THE REAL FINDING. The budget record is written only by served runs, source live-run in every reading here. A hold blocks every run. So once a hold is recorded, nothing in the ordinary path can ever clear it: the only writer is the thing the hold forbids. It is the same bootstrap shape the concurrency plan already recorded for the watcher guard — watch exits on an empty project while dispatch refuses without a watcher, so the first dispatch of a wave can never have one — and it means this section's third measure, a probe writes back, is not a convenience for saving a duplicate probe. It is the deadlock's only exit, and should be stated that way. A second defect surfaced beside it: there is no waiver for a budget hold. Every other fence in this surface carries a recorded escape — allow-unreconciled-runs, no-watch, waive-suite-delta, waive-boundary-refusal, allow-execution-mismatch — and §6 of clive-local-workers records what happens when a guard has none, where a wrong verdict blocked six runs across three sessions for an hour because it could not be overridden. A stale hold with no override is that incident's shape a second time. The wave was routed to the local lane, which is unmetered and therefore never subject to this, and the two monitor nodes are running there.

reckon-ship · 2026-09-03T13:26:00+00:00

THE RECORD IS HISTORY, THE POLL IS THE AUTHORITY — the lead's inversion, and it supersedes the ladder's ordering above. This section had the written record as primary with a probe as a staleness escape hatch. That is backwards, and today settles it: the record was wrong in BOTH directions on the same afternoon. The claude lane read HELD at 100 per cent on evidence stamped 10:02:01Z while the pre-flight ran at 13:21:40Z, three hours nineteen minutes stale, and a live probe at that moment was served — seventeen consecutive dispatches were routed away from a working lane. Its sibling read CLEAR on evidence from 06:23:58Z, seven hours older still, and happened to be right. Something that can be wrong in either direction is not an authority; it is a log, and which reading blocks a wave was luck. SO THE DESIGN INVERTS. A wave's availability is decided by polling the lane. The record keeps what was observed, when, and by which rung — for calibration, for reporting, and for the four axes — and gates nothing. A reading may be reused within a wave under a declared short cache life measured in seconds or a minute, and such a reuse is a CACHE carrying its age rather than a verdict; nothing hours old ever decides anything. THE COST IS MEASURED AND IT SETS THE GRANULARITY, which is the one place this needs care. Two probes today cost 0.37658 and 0.37927 US dollars each. That is not the two-token prompt; it is 28,922 to 40,470 tokens of cache creation, because a probe pays to build the prompt cache from cold. So a probe is cheap per WAVE and not cheap per NODE: at roughly a hundred nodes in a day, per-node polling is about thirty-eight dollars while per-wave polling is cents. Poll when a wave opens, cache for the wave, and let a node inherit the wave's reading. Two cheaper rungs remain available and both are already noted here: auth_check, declared for none of the nine backends, answers reachability at zero tokens and never quota; and the rate-limit telemetry every served request already returns updates the log for free, which is what makes the log good history and still not an authority.

ROOT CAUSE OF GONE WITHOUT A COMPLETE MANIFEST, AND THE CLASSIFIER IS NOT AT FAULT. The lead reported the note recurring on a peer project's pane at 17:23:35 and 17:25:11, on two sonnet runs. Both were measured directly from their run directories and the verdict is accurate in both: the process is gone and there is no complete manifest. The defect is one layer upstream and there are TWO MECHANISMS behind the one message. MECHANISM ONE, THE HARNESS BACKGROUND-WAIT CEILING. The run n-drain-closes-the-detachment-tail wrote to its stderr: 'Background tasks still running after 600s; terminating. Set CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0 to wait indefinitely.' Its final result record is a clean turn - subtype success, is_error false, stop_reason end_turn, three turns - carrying the text 'Continuing to wait for pool-level (compose/review) activity from the drain.' So the worker finished a turn while waiting on background work it had started, and the harness killed the process group at a six hundred second ceiling before any later turn could write a manifest. Three runs across two days carry that stderr line. MECHANISM TWO, AND IT NEEDS NO CEILING AT ALL. The run n-callers-pass-the-run-to-the-detachment has an EMPTY stderr, fifty-six turns, and a final result reading 'Waiting for the background full tests/standard_names suite run to complete before finalizing the manifest.' Nothing terminated it. It ended its turn intending to be given another one, and a print-mode invocation has no next turn - the process exits when the model emits end_turn. The worker's plan required a future that its own process lifetime does not contain. THE COMMON CAUSE, which is the sentence worth keeping: A WORKER TREATS A BACKGROUND TASK AS SOMETHING IT CAN WAIT ACROSS, WHILE ITS PROCESS LIFETIME ENDS WITH ITS TURN. The ceiling is only the variant where the wait lasts long enough to be killed; the end-of-turn exit is the same error arriving sooner and more quietly. AND THE EVIDENCE IS ON DISK AND NOTHING READS IT, which is the seventh instance in this repository of a record carrying the fact while its consumer discards it. A grep for the ceiling string, and for the environment key it names, across the whole of reckon returns nothing. The stderr file sits beside the stream in every run directory and the final result record carries the worker's own account of what it was waiting for; the classifier reads neither, so it reports the true but useless fact that a manifest is absent instead of the actionable one that the run was waiting on background work and can be resumed. TWO FIXES, DISPATCHED SEPARATELY BECAUSE THEY ARE DETECTION AND PREVENTION. Detection, on the recovery classifier: a run whose stderr names the background-wait ceiling, or whose final result text says it was waiting on background work, classifies as its own outcome naming the wait, and the disposition tells a coordinator to resume rather than redispatch - because in both measured cases the session is intact and a resume would have collected the manifest. Prevention, on the dispatch contract: the contract must state that a worker's process ends with its turn, so a manifest is written BEFORE any background wait begins and updated after, never deferred until the wait completes. That rule already exists in this workstation's guidance for multi-hour campaigns, as launch then harvest with incremental checkpoints, and the two measured runs show it is needed at the scale of a single test suite rather than only a slurm job.

impl-attrib · 2026-09-03T16:00:35.813Z

reckon-ship · 2026-09-03T18:10:00+00:00

A SEAT RECORD OUTLIVES ITS PROCESS, FOUND IN A WORKTREE AUDIT RATHER THAN IN A RUN. Closing this session's worktrees turned up nineteen trees, thirteen clean and reachable and removed, five holding uncommitted duplicates of work already landed, and ONE holding a capability that reached no commit and exists nowhere in the tree. Its symbol is absent from every file in reckon and tests, so it was never merged and would have been lost with the worktree. THE CAPABILITY IS A LIVENESS FIX AND IT BELONGS TO THIS SECTION'S FAMILY. The liveness check reads a seat record, confirms the pid against the process table and the recorded start time, and returns the verdict - and when the answer is dead it leaves the record in place. The unlanded work erases that record at the moment the process is confirmed gone, writing the same payload an explicit unwatch writes, lock-free and best-effort so that a concurrent arming or teardown is never clobbered. Its own docstring states the reason better than a summary would: the record is what a reader trusts between arming and process death, and left alone it keeps answering a question the process table has already contradicted. THAT SENTENCE IS THE DAY'S RECURRING DEFECT IN ITS SHORTEST FORM, and it now has four measured faces on this workstation. In every case a stored answer outlived the thing it described, and in every case the correction is the same: a record that cannot be re-derived must carry when it was written, and a consumer must consult that before treating it as current. a-stale-hold-is-probed-not-obeyed — delivered report

"""Budget-aware dispatch — hold a wave rather than burn it into a spent quota.

An orchestrator running unattended waves against metered backends will
eventually launch into an exhausted quota, and that failure is expensive in a
specific way: the worktrees already exist, the nodes are already fenced, and the
work is already part done, so the loss is not one rejected call but a whole
wave's setup plus half-finished commits somebody has to judge. Holding *before*
a wave costs nothing by comparison, which is the whole argument for this module.

Three rules shape it, and each one exists because its opposite fails.

**Unknown never blocks; only recorded exhaustion holds.** The backends disagree
about what they publish, so a block showing no headroom is indistinguishable, on
any single field, from one showing plenty. Reading silence as exhaustion would
make the system refuse to work on whichever backend happens to publish least —
an invisible failure that stalls everything, where the reactive failure it was
trying to avoid is cheap and announces itself.

**A newer silence never overwrites an older measurement.** An observation
carrying no headroom carries no information, so the latest *known* reading is the
state, and it decays only through its own reset time. A successfully completed
run is different: its trustworthy completion stamp proves that the backend
served, so it can displace an earlier exhaustion without inventing a utilisation
figure. Taking every other "most recent" silence at face value would let one
quiet record erase a real exhaustion and open the wave this module exists to
hold.

**An undated refusal is probed, not timed.** A refusal naming a reset remains
stronger evidence until that time. One naming no reset cannot say when the lane
will serve again, so an opted-in backend receives one minimal serving request.
Its bounded per-backend cache turns a wave of callers into one request. Where a
host cannot make that request, the declared shelf life remains the fallback.

A hold is never destructive and never silent. It creates no worktree, fails no
node and cancels nothing; the nodes stay ready. It reports which backend, at what
utilisation, and when that resets — because a hold that looks like silence is
indistinguishable from a crashed orchestrator, and because the reset time is what
lets the wave resume without a human.

A pre-flight also names the pace it is judging a wave inside, so a coordinator
reads it before committing rather than discovering it in a refusal. Per declared
budget group it reports both metered clocks with the age of each reading, the
allowance derived from the week that group has to last, and the bar a stated
ready set is judged against — each figure carried with the observation it came
from, because a utilisation that cannot be aged cannot be told from a current
one. A group no reading reached reports unknown for its clocks and its allowance
rather than a zero, which is the first rule above applied to a second quantity.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, Mapping

from reckon import _backends, crew, ledger
from reckon._timestamps import parse_utc
from reckon.crew import bar as bar_module
from reckon.crew import budget_group, window_reading
from reckon.crew import pace as pace_module
from reckon.crew import reserve as reserve_module
from reckon.crew import rollout as rollout_module
from reckon.crew.refusals import format_refusal

# What a pre-flight is deciding about. The two differ only in whether the resume
# reserve applies: withholding headroom from a fresh dispatch is the point of the
# reserve, and withholding it from the resumption the reserve exists to protect
# would defeat it.
PURPOSES = ("dispatch", "resume")

# Used when no config layer supplied a policy value. Deliberately permissive
# rather than a mirror of the shipped defaults: the shipped layer is where real
# defaults live so that resolution can report which layer set each key, and a
# second copy here would be indistinguishable from a value nobody ever set.
UNSET_CEILING_PCT = 100.0
UNSET_RESERVE_PCT = 0.0

# How long a recorded exhaustion that names no reset time keeps describing now.
# This one is a real default rather than a permissive placeholder, because the
# permissive reading is the defect: a judgement carrying no reset decays through
# nothing, so an hour-old refusal and a day-old one hold a lane identically and
# for as long as the record survives. The hold cannot clear itself either — only
# a served run writes a budget record, and the hold refuses every run — so the
# lane is unreachable by the one thing that would update it. Nor can a reader
# override it: a refusal records full utilisation and the ceiling is capped at
# the same figure, so the comparison refuses under every permitted setting.
#
# An hour balances the two costs this module already weighs against each other.
# It is longer than a wave takes to rediscover a genuine refusal — which is
# cheap, announces itself, and writes a fresh record as it does so — and it is a
# fraction of the shortest metered window measured, so a lane that really is
# spent is re-recorded by the very dispatch that tests it. Set the key to zero
# or less to disable ageing and keep the indefinite hold.
DEFAULT_SHELF_LIFE_MINUTES = 60.0
DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY_PROBE_CACHE_SECONDS = 60.0

# Provider utilisation is reported as an integer percentage. At 1.69% of a
# window, one percentage point changes the burn multiple by 1 / 1.69 = 0.59,
# so an opening-hours projection would mostly measure quantisation. Waiting for
# 5% elapsed caps that step at 0.2x; requiring 5% used gives the reading at
# least five integer samples, so one point is at most 20% of measured use.
BURN_ELAPSED_FRACTION_FLOOR = 0.05
BURN_UTILISATION_PCT_FLOOR = 5.0

# The account's own severity labels that mean a window is raised. Severity is
# the account's server-computed posture rather than a threshold reckon invents,
# so a raised label holds even when a numeric utilisation alone would sit under
# the configured ceiling: the fence holds no looser than the figure the account
# reports, whichever of the two inputs is currently telling the truth.
RAISED_SEVERITIES = ("warning", "critical")


@dataclass
class BudgetState:
    """What is known about one backend's remaining headroom, and how.

    ``source`` and ``observed_at`` are part of the answer rather than
    bookkeeping: a caller deciding whether to hold a wave needs to know whether
    the figure came from a run that finished minutes ago or from a record that
    has since reset.
    """

    backend: str
    headroom: str = "unknown"
    utilisation_pct: float | None = None
    burn_multiple: float | None = None
    projected_exhaustion_at: str | None = None
    rate_limit_type: str | None = None
    rate_limit_period_minutes: float | None = None
    resets_at: str | None = None
    seconds_until_reset: int | None = None
    threshold_status: str | None = None
    severity: str | None = None
    observed_at: str | None = None
    age_source: str | None = None
    source: str = "none"
    expired: bool = False
    detail: str = ""
    availability: str | None = None
    availability_observed_at: str | None = None
    availability_cached: bool = False

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return the state as sorted JSON-ready data."""
        return {
            "backend": self.backend,
            "burn_multiple": self.burn_multiple,
            "availability": self.availability,
            "availability_cached": self.availability_cached,
            "availability_observed_at": self.availability_observed_at,
            "age_source": self.age_source,
            "detail": self.detail,
            "expired": self.expired,
            "headroom": self.headroom,
            "observed_at": self.observed_at,
            "projected_exhaustion_at": self.projected_exhaustion_at,
            "rate_limit_period_minutes": self.rate_limit_period_minutes,
            "rate_limit_type": self.rate_limit_type,
            "resets_at": self.resets_at,
            "seconds_until_reset": self.seconds_until_reset,
            "source": self.source,
            "threshold_status": self.threshold_status,
            "severity": self.severity,
            "utilisation_pct": self.utilisation_pct,
        }


# ── Policy ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def policy(config: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Read the thresholds that decide a hold out of flight config.

    The shelf life is one of them, and it governs only a judgement that states
    no reset time. One that states a reset already names its own decay and is
    left to it, so the two mechanisms never both apply to the same record.
    """
    block = (config or {}).get("budget") or {}
    ceiling = block.get("utilisation_ceiling_pct")
    reserve = block.get("resume_reserve_pct")
    coordinator_reserve = block.get("coordinator_reserve_pct")
    statuses = block.get("exhausted_statuses") or ()
    shelf_life = block.get("evidence_shelf_life_minutes")
    resolved = {
        "utilisation_ceiling_pct": (
            UNSET_CEILING_PCT if ceiling is None else float(ceiling)
        ),
        "resume_reserve_pct": UNSET_RESERVE_PCT if reserve is None else float(reserve),
        "coordinator_reserve_pct": (
            UNSET_RESERVE_PCT
            if coordinator_reserve is None
            else float(coordinator_reserve)
        ),
        "exhausted_statuses": [str(status) for status in statuses],
        "evidence_shelf_life_minutes": (
            DEFAULT_SHELF_LIFE_MINUTES if shelf_life is None else float(shelf_life)
        ),
    }
    resolved["availability_probe_cache_seconds"] = availability_probe_cache_seconds(
        resolved
    )
    return resolved


def availability_probe_cache_seconds(policy_block: Mapping[str, Any]) -> float:
    """Bound probe reuse by the configured shelf life and the short default."""
    shelf_seconds = max(
        0.0,
        float(
            policy_block.get("evidence_shelf_life_minutes", DEFAULT_SHELF_LIFE_MINUTES)
        )
        * 60.0,
    )
    return min(DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY_PROBE_CACHE_SECONDS, shelf_seconds)


def effective_ceiling(policy_block: Mapping[str, Any], purpose: str) -> float:
    """Return the utilisation a dispatch of this purpose will not cross.

    A fresh dispatch stops at the ceiling less the reserves; answering a worker
    that stopped and asked for help may spend them, because that is the exact
    expenditure the reserves were withheld for. The coordinator reserve keeps
    headroom for the coordinator that must survive the wave to audit manifests,
    merge commits and record outcomes; a wave that spends it on a new node
    strands the wave in its worst state — work in flight and nothing left to
    unblock or close it with.
    """
    ceiling = float(policy_block.get("utilisation_ceiling_pct", UNSET_CEILING_PCT))
    if purpose == "resume":
        return ceiling
    resume = float(policy_block.get("resume_reserve_pct", UNSET_RESERVE_PCT))
    coordinator = float(policy_block.get("coordinator_reserve_pct", UNSET_RESERVE_PCT))
    return max(0.0, ceiling - resume - coordinator)


def withheld_reserves(policy_block: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    """Name each nonzero reserve a fresh dispatch is withheld by.

    The reason a hold carries must say which headroom was withheld, or a reader
    who sees a lane stop below the ceiling cannot tell what was protecting whom.
    """
    labels = (
        ("resume_reserve_pct", "resume reserve"),
        ("coordinator_reserve_pct", "coordinator reserve"),
    )
    withheld = []
    for key, label in labels:
        value = float(policy_block.get(key, 0.0) or 0.0)
        if value > 0:
            withheld.append(f"{value:g}% {label}")
    return withheld


# ── Reading what was already recorded ───────────────────────────────────────


def _now(now: datetime | None = None) -> datetime:
    return now or datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc)


def _parse_stamp(value: Any) -> datetime | None:
    """Parse an ISO-8601 stamp, returning None for anything unreadable.

    Only a string is a stamp: a number, ``None`` or any other object reads as
    nothing. The shared parser is tolerant of surrounding space and of a
    lowercase zone designator; this reader's recorded contract refuses both, so
    a string whose own text is not spelled strictly reads as unreadable.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return None
    if value != value.strip() or value.endswith("z"):
        return None
    return parse_utc(value)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Reading:
    """One recorded budget block with the backend and moment it belongs to."""

    backend: str | None
    budget: dict[str, Any]
    observed_at: str
    when: datetime
    source: str
    age_source: str
    record_id: str = ""
    attribution: str = ""
    surface_opt_in: bool = False
    covered_backends: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    served_completion: bool = False

    def applies_to(self, backend_name: str) -> bool:
        """Return whether this reading explicitly describes ``backend_name``."""
        if self.backend == backend_name:
            return True
        return backend_name in self.covered_backends


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _RefusalEvent:
    """The newest stream refusal and any later provider-side refutation."""

    stamp: str | None
    served_status: str | None = None


class _RecordedReadings(dict[str, _Reading]):
    """Best reading per backend plus signals whose owner is still unknown."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        best: Mapping[str, _Reading],
        *,
        unattributed: Iterable[_Reading] = (),
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(best)
        self.unattributed = tuple(unattributed)

    def for_backend(self, backend_name: str) -> _Reading | None:
        """Resolve one backend to its own reading or one declared coverage."""
        direct = self.get(backend_name)
        if direct is not None and direct.backend == backend_name:
            return direct
